quotes.quote: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 incorporates 9 evaluations: AA-Briefcase v1.1, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf, FrontierCode-AA 2.0, Terminal-Bench 4.0, AA-Omniscience v1.1, HLE-Diamond, CritPt v2 (Hard Subset), and Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1.0.

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is a primarily text-based, English-language evaluation suite. Models that accept image input also receive images in some of its evaluations, such as the HLE-Diamond image questions and GDP.pdf page images.
We benchmark visual reasoning, speech inputs and multilingual performance separately from the Intelligence Index.
Like all evaluation metrics, it has limitations and may not apply directly to every use case.
We use e2b as our primary sandbox provider for agentic benchmarks.

Rubric grading and the analytical-quality and presentation pairwise comparisons each use a panel of three judges rather than a single judge, reducing bias toward submissions from the same model or model family.

The Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average across four categories: Knowledge Work (25%), Coding (25%), Science (25%), and General (25%). Category membership and per-evaluation weights are shown below.
Temperature: 0 for non-reasoning models, 0.6 for reasoning models (unless another temperature is recommended by the model lab)

We generally use pass@1 scoring across our evaluations, where a model must produce the correct answer on its first attempt. For evaluations with multiple repeats, pass@1 is calculated by aggregating results across all repeats.
Automatic retry on API failures (up to 30 attempts)
Rebalanced category weights: Knowledge Work (25%), Coding (25%), Science (25%), General (25%)

Adjusted category weights to further emphasize agentic tasks: Agents (34%), Coding (24%), Scientific Reasoning (24%), General (18%), with AA-Omniscience split into Accuracy (8%) and Non-Hallucination (4%) components
New category-based weighting structure: Agents (25%), Coding (25%), General (25%), Scientific Reasoning (25%)
Removed MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench, and AIME 2025 from the Intelligence Index
Added Terminal-Bench Hard (agentic workflows)
Renamed the Agents category to Knowledge Work and Scientific Reasoning to Science, and moved GDP.pdf into Knowledge Work
Reduced the GDP.pdf weight from 10% to 5%
Incorporated grading robustness improvements from the CritPt authors and regraded all models on CritPt v2

For inclusion in the Intelligence Index, the combined AA-Briefcase v1.1 Elo is frozen at the time of a model's addition and normalized as clamp((Elo - 500) / 2000). The Elo scale is anchored to GPT-5.5 (medium) at 1000
Artificial Analysis may update the reference parameters as models progress against the evaluation, to maintain meaningful differentiation in the Intelligence Index.
Models are evaluated on multi-week knowledge work projects, each with many linked tasks and thousands of input source files.

AA-Omniscience contributes two components to the Intelligence Index: (1) Accuracy - the proportion of correct answers, weighted at 10% of the overall Index, and (2) Non-Hallucination Rate - calculated as 1 minus the hallucination rate, weighted at 5% of the overall Index
The AA-Omniscience v1.1 dataset has 3,000 questions, down from 6,000 in the original AA-Omniscience dataset.

Evaluation set: 100 tasks across ten professional domains, grounded in 4,592 PDF pages and graded against 1,275 criteria. We attempt every task five times, so each model has a fixed denominator of 500 attempts.
All-pass is the headline metric: the share of all 500 attempts where every criterion passes.
We evaluate the full Terminal-Bench 4.0 dataset (66 tasks) using the mini-swe-agent harness, with pass@1 scoring averaged over 3 repeats per task

We evaluate the full Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1.0 release (70 tasks: 19 life sciences, 17 physical sciences, 17 mathematical sciences, 9 engineering sciences, 8 earth sciences) using the mini-swe-agent harness, with pass@1 scoring averaged over 3 repeats per task

The hard subset of CritPt v2 is a fixed, private list of 40 of the 70 CritPt problems, selected to remove the 30 problems that seven frontier models solved in all five attempts at the time CritPt v2 was launched.
An attempt that fails any blocking check, or that the trajectory scanner flags for looking up the solution, scores 0.
We evaluate a private 657-task held-out split from AutomationBench dataset version 1.0.6
Models without image input receive only the question text for the 272 image questions, and we grade them on all 1,000 questions
A composite benchmark aggregating nine challenging evaluations to provide a holistic measure of AI capabilities across knowledge work, coding, science, and general knowledge.
All evaluations are conducted independently by Artificial Analysis.
Objective: Create a single-page LaTeX document containing a TikZ diagram that maps the structure of the New Zealand egg market.
Instruction: We have an e-commerce app API server running locally at http://main:8080, currently backed by MySQL.

Reconstruct, from the bundled satellite imagery alone, the freeze-up date and the ice-off date of the lake described below, for each of the ten winters 2013-14, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2016-17, 2017-18, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23 and 2023-24.
In ECMAScript 2025, what JavaScript string literal does RegExp.escape(' ') return? Answer using a JS string literal (i.e., with backslashes escaped).

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is calculated as a weighted average of production benchmark scores, scaled from 0 to 100. Four categories each contribute 25%: Knowledge Work, Coding, Science, and General.

Claude Fable 5.2 (Max, Default Fallback) currently has the highest Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index score, with a score of 65 among models with published Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index results.

A higher score indicates stronger aggregate performance across the benchmark suite, but individual benchmark results may be more relevant for specific use cases such as coding, agentic workflows, factuality, or scientific reasoning.
With v5, 60% of the Index is now based on evaluations with private test sets or held-out answers.
Claude Opus 5.5 (max) leads at 58, ahead of GPT-6 Astra (max, 57) and GPT-6.1 Sol (max, 55): Anthropic and OpenAI hold the top five models. Gemini 4 Argon (high) is next at 50

Kimi K3.1 Pro (weights not yet released) is the top open weights model at 46. Among released weights, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 (max) and GLM-5.3 (max) lead at 32 - 26 points behind the leader and below Claude Haiku 5.5 (max, 36)
Effort settings matter more in v5 than in v4.3. Claude Opus 5.5 scores 35 at low effort and 58 at max, at 10x the cost per Intelligence Index task ($0.98 vs $10.04).

v5 leaves significant room for progress across all nine evaluations, and no single model leads them all. Of the models we measured, Claude Opus 5.5 leads three, and five other models lead the remaining six:
Staying in the Index: AA-Briefcase, AutomationBench-AA, GDP.pdf and Terminal-Bench 4.0
Removed IFBench due to saturation. The benchmark no longer distinguishes frontier models sufficiently, so we have removed it from the Intelligence Index.
The upgrade re-baselines Elo to human performance at 1000, introduces a rotating panel of frontier-model judges, and raises the turn limit from 100 to 250 for longer-horizon agent trajectories
Full Intelligence Index v4.1 weights:

Claude Fable 5 (with Opus 4.8 fallback, 60) leads the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1 by four points but is currently unavailable, leaving Claude Opus 4.8 (max, 56) as the most intelligent available model, ahead of GPT-5.5 (xhigh, 55)
HLE, AA-LCR and AA-Omniscience are now graded by GPT-5.6 Luna (medium), replacing GPT-4o, Qwen3 235B A22B 2507, and Gemini 3 Flash Preview respectively.
Published scores are now using v4.1.1, so all model results on Artificial Analysis now reflect these changes and use our latest consistent, independent methodology.
We have been planning and building elements of Index v5 for months - it’s been 8 months since we launched Index v4 in January.
GPQA Diamond, an exceptional scientific reasoning evaluation that has now been saturated
Index v4.2 has more complex and realistic tasks, and more private test sets to prevent gaming
plus greater weighting on held-out test sets to prevent gaming, and grading infrastructure upgrades to increase robustness
We are upgrading Terminal-Bench to 4.0 and adding AutomationBench-AA, an agentic workflow automation benchmark with a private test set.
Because we use a held-out test set for AutomationBench in collaboration with Zapier, the weight assigned to evaluations with private tasks or answers increases from 40% to 45%.
Category weights are unchanged from v4.2: Agents 30%, Coding 20%, General 30%, Scientific Reasoning 20%.

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3 incorporates 10 evaluations: AA-Briefcase, GDPval-AA v2, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, SciCode, Humanity's Last Exam, GDP.pdf, CritPt, AA-Omniscience, AA-LCR v1.1
Each change in v4.2 and v4.3 stands on its own merits and brings the index closer to real-world problem solving, adds more private test sets to prevent gaming, and reduces saturation.
We run all 66 tasks three times and report average pass@1.
Incorporated grading robustness improvements from the CritPt authors and regraded all models on CritPt v2.

Artificial Analysis is the independent benchmarking company for AI. We measure the agents and models, the clouds that serve them, and the chips they run on, helping developers and companies optimize the entire AI stack.
Micah Hill-Smith is Co-Founder and CEO of Artificial Analysis, based in San Francisco.
George Cameron is based out of San Francisco, California and is the CPO and Co-Founder of Artificial Analysis.

The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is designed to measure current frontier capability. Its composition is updated periodically: evaluations are added as models improve, and evaluations that no longer differentiate leading models are retired.
Each version of the Intelligence Index is therefore measured on a different set of evaluations, and scores across versions are not intended for long-run comparison.
